stem: An energy company offers three monthly electricity plans. For \(x\) kilowatt-hours (kWh) used in a month, the costs in dollars are:

Plan A: a fixed charge of $18 plus $0.28 per kWh. Plan B: a fixed charge of $45 plus $0.22 per kWh. Plan C: no fixed charge; $0.40 per kWh for the first 200 kWh, and $0.20 per kWh for every kWh after that.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the cost of using 300 kWh in a month on plan A and on plan B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of kWh for which plans A and B cost the same.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the cost on plan C of using (i) 150 kWh; (ii) 500 kWh.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Show that, for \(x > 200\), the cost on plan C is \(C(x) = 0.2x + 40\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the range of values of \(x\) for which plan A is cheaper than both of the other plans.

parts.label: f
parts.text: A household on plan C paid $150 for one month. Find the number of kWh it used.

idea: Plans A and B are linear models: fixed charge plus a rate times \(x\). Plan C is piecewise: one rule up to 200 kWh and another above. Compare plans by finding where their costs are equal.

solution.label: d
steps: The first 200 kWh cost $80, and the other \(x - 200\) cost $0.20 each: \(80 + 0.2(x - 200) = 0.2x + 40\).

solution.label: e
steps: For \(x \le 200\): C costs \(0.4x\), and \(0.4x > 18 + 0.28x\) when \(x > 150\). So A is cheaper than C for \(150 < x \le 200\).
A is cheaper than B for \(x < 450\), which covers all of these values.

solution.label: f
steps: $150 is more than the $80 for the first 200 kWh, so use \(0.2x + 40 = 150\).

stem: The temperature inside a cold-storage room, \(T\) °C, \(t\) minutes after the cooling unit switches on is modelled by \[T(t) = 1.5\sin(20t) + 4, \quad t \ge 0,\] where \(20t\) is in degrees.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the highest and the lowest temperature in the room.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the period of the model.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the temperature 10 minutes after the unit switches on.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the two times in the first 18 minutes at which the temperature is 5 °C.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the length of time in each cycle for which the temperature is above 5 °C, and write it as a percentage of the cycle.

parts.label: f
parts.text: An engineer changes the model to \(T(t) = a\sin(bt) + 4\), so that the highest temperature is 4.8 °C and one cycle takes 12 minutes, where \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\). Find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).

idea: For \(a\sin(bx) + d\): the amplitude is \(a\), the principal axis is \(y = d\), and the period is \(\dfrac{360}{b}\) in degrees. Equations such as \(T(t) = 5\) are solved with the calculator, or from the graph.

solution.label: e
steps: Above 5 °C between the two times: \(6.909\ldots - 2.090\ldots = 4.818\ldots\) minutes.

stem: A curved garden path is modelled by a quadratic \(y = ax^{2} + bx + c\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are distances in metres. The path passes through the points \((0, 2)\), \((4, 6)\) and \((12, 4.4)\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down three equations in \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the values of \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the vertex of the path.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A straight hedge follows the line \(y = 0.25x + 2\). Find the \(x\)-coordinates of the points where the hedge meets the path.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Between these two points, the path is above the hedge. Find the greatest vertical distance between them.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The path runs from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 14\). Find the range of \(y\) for the path.

parts.label: g
parts.text: A lamp post stands at the point \((8, 3)\). Determine whether it is in the region between the path and the hedge.

idea: Each point on the curve gives one linear equation in \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\). The vertical distance between the path and the hedge is the difference of their \(y\)-values, itself a quadratic, whose greatest value is at its vertex.

solution.label: a
steps: Substitute each point into \(y = ax^{2} + bx + c\).

solution.label: e
steps: Vertical distance: \(d = -0.1x^{2} + 1.15x\). Its vertex is at \(x = \dfrac{1.15}{0.2} = 5.75\).

solution.label: f
steps: The greatest value is 6.9 at the vertex. At the ends, \(y(0) = 2\) and \(y(14) = -19.6 + 19.6 + 2 = 2\).

solution.label: g
steps: At \(x = 8\) the hedge is at \(y = 4\) and the path at \(y = 6.8\). The lamp post is at \(y = 3\), below the hedge.
solution.answer: No: it is below the hedge, outside the region

stem: Phone X is put on charge. Its battery level, as a percentage, \(t\) minutes later is modelled by \[B(t) = 100 - 85(0.92)^{t}, \quad t \ge 0.\]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the battery level when the phone is put on charge.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the battery level after 10 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time it takes for the battery level to reach 80 %.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Write down the equation of the horizontal asymptote of the graph of \(B\), and explain what it means for the battery.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Phone Y starts at 20 % and charges at a steady 2.5 percentage points per minute until it is full. Write down a model \(Y(t)\) for its battery level, with its domain, and state the time at which it is full.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The two phones are put on charge at the same time. Find the two times at which they have the same battery level.

parts.label: g
parts.text: Determine which phone reaches 95 % first.

idea: In \(100 - 85(0.92)^{t}\) the term \(85(0.92)^{t}\) gets smaller and smaller but never reaches 0, so \(B\) approaches 100 without reaching it. Compare an exponential and a linear model by solving \(B(t) = Y(t)\) with the calculator.

solution.label: d
solution.answer: \(y = 100\): the battery gets closer and closer to full but, in the model, never quite reaches 100 %

solution.label: f
steps: Solve \(100 - 85(0.92)^{t} = 20 + 2.5t\) with the calculator, for \(0 \le t \le 32\): \(t = 1.176\ldots\) and \(t = 28.96\ldots\)

solution.label: g
solution.answer: Phone Y, after 30 minutes (phone X takes 34.0 minutes)

stem: A group of volunteers clears litter from a beach. The time the job takes, \(T\) hours, varies inversely with the number of volunteers, \(n\), so \(T = \dfrac{k}{n}\). Six volunteers take 6 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of \(k\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time the job takes with 9 volunteers.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe what happens to \(T\) as \(n\) increases, and write down the equation of the horizontal asymptote of the graph of \(T\) against \(n\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Each volunteer is paid $15 for travel, and the organiser pays $40 for each hour the job takes. Show that the total cost, \(C\) dollars, is \(C(n) = 15n + \dfrac{1440}{n}\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Use your calculator to find the whole number of volunteers that makes the cost as small as possible, and the smallest cost.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The job must be finished in at most 3 hours. Find the least number of volunteers needed, and the cost.

parts.label: g
parts.text: Find the greatest and least cost for groups of 4 to 20 volunteers.

idea: Inverse variation \(T = \dfrac{k}{n}\) means that doubling \(n\) halves \(T\). The cost adds a part that grows with \(n\) (travel) to a part that shrinks as \(n\) grows (hours of the job), so it has a least value in between; \(n\) must be a whole number.

solution.label: c
steps: As \(n\) gets larger, \(\dfrac{36}{n}\) gets smaller and closer to 0, but never reaches it.

solution.label: d
steps: Travel: \(15n\). The job takes \(\dfrac{36}{n}\) hours, costing \(40 \times \dfrac{36}{n} = \dfrac{1440}{n}\).

solution.label: e
steps: The graph of \(C\) has its minimum at \(n = 9.797\ldots\), which is not a whole number. Compare the whole numbers either side: \(C(9) = 135 + 160 = 295\) and \(C(10) = 150 + 144 = 294\).

solution.label: g
steps: The least cost is $294 (part (e)). At the ends: \(C(4) = 60 + 360 = 420\) and \(C(20) = 300 + 72 = 372\).

stem: A school stall bakes and sells cookies at a fair. The cost of making \(x\) cookies is \(C(x) = 40 + 0.6x\) dollars, and the income from selling them is \(R(x) = 2.4x - 0.004x^{2}\) dollars, for \(0 \le x \le 600\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the fixed cost.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the profit is \(P(x) = -0.004x^{2} + 1.8x - 40\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the least and the greatest whole number of cookies the stall can sell and still make a profit.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the number of cookies that gives the greatest profit, and the greatest profit.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The price of each cookie is \(\dfrac{R(x)}{x}\). Find the price that gives the greatest profit.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The oven can bake at most 200 cookies. Find the greatest profit now.

parts.label: g
parts.text: Find the range of \(P\) for \(0 \le x \le 600\).

idea: Profit is income minus cost. The stall makes a profit between the two zeros of the quadratic \(P\), and the greatest profit is at the vertex, unless the vertex is outside the values allowed.

solution.label: c
steps: A profit needs \(P(x) > 0\), so between the two. The number of cookies is a whole number.

solution.label: f
steps: The vertex, 225, is more than 200, and \(P\) is increasing for \(x < 225\), so the best is \(x = 200\).

solution.label: g
steps: The greatest value is 162.5 at the vertex. At the ends, \(P(0) = -40\) and \(P(600) = -1440 + 1080 - 40 = -400\).
